entry_state: Chapter 3 has specified source assertions, coverage, mapping, information views and dependency-sensitive corrections. A revised conclusion cannot rewrite a committed event or authorize a new correcting journal without the applicable treatment. The literature chapter must now explain which existing methods support these requirements and where their boundaries lie.
exit_state: The literature supplies scoped accounting structures, provenance, partial-identification methods, rule languages, extraction tools and solvers. None alone supplies the complete disclosure-to-history-to-event-to-journal argument. Integration, a fair typed-library comparison and empirical advantage remain to be established; the next chapter must explain the proposed architecture and its division of responsibilities.
findings: The completed rendered reading of pages 74–79 is recorded from the saved continuation state; it covers the entire literature chapter in order.

Each literature family has an explicit application boundary: conservation does not select transactions, provenance is not probability, extraction accuracy is not financial meaning, and solver success does not establish history coverage.
The typed-library/shared-IR competitor remains live. REA and Caiani acquisition gaps do not supply imported technical claims.
TableFormer structure prediction, supplied PDF text, correction procedures and descriptive TEDS scores remain distinct. The reviewed grammar changes read correctly in context.
No new confirmed defect; rendered text was legible without clipping. The sparse final page completes the integration argument.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.entry_belief: The historical record needs both accounting consistency and economic state.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.open_question: Which existing accounting and company models support those needs?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.parent_contribution: Conservation, syntax and stock-flow precedents are related to the proposed company representation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.belief_update: These precedents supply structures whose data, behavioural and reporting assumptions still require local justification.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.exit_question: How should the representation retain facts that remain unknown?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.removal_verdict: Removing this section would obscure the distinction between conserving balances and identifying permissible transactions.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.swap_verdict: Accounting and company dynamics appropriately precede methods for their incomplete observation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.entry_verdict: The conservation example recalls why balanced journals alone were insufficient in Chapter 1.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.exit_verdict: REA and Caiani remain acquisition gaps instead of silently supporting technical claims.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.promise_verdict: The section identifies usable precedents without claiming automatic public-filing reconstruction.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.distinct_contribution_verdict: Its stock-flow and calibration qualifications concern financial dynamics rather than extraction or inference.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.entry_belief: Observed accounting records leave dependent unknowns and multiple versions.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.open_question: What database ideas preserve these unknowns without inventing probabilities?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.parent_contribution: Conditional tables, certain answers, provenance and time semantics support historical representation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.belief_update: Shared symbols retain dependence, while provenance and certain-answer results have specified query-language limits.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.exit_question: What additional assumptions are required to place distributions over compatible histories?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.removal_verdict: Without this section, later families and information views would lose their database foundations and limitations.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.swap_verdict: It must precede probability because explaining dependence does not yet assign a measure.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.entry_verdict: Incomplete information connects directly to the retained alternatives in the preceding company cases.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.exit_verdict: Valid/storage time is distinguished from the public availability needed by investors.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.promise_verdict: The text explains positive relational provenance without extending it to arbitrary negation or optimisation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.distinct_contribution_verdict: It preserves the difference between a derivation trace, an answer true in every model, and probability.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.entry_belief: A compatible set can preserve unknowns without supplying a probability law.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.open_question: How do inverse problems and partial identification delimit probabilistic claims?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.parent_contribution: The section separates information identified by observations from assumptions used to weight histories.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.belief_update: Priors, likelihoods and model spaces are additional choices; duplicate encodings cannot legitimately acquire extra mass.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.exit_question: How can executable rules represent the alternatives whose weights remain conditional?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.removal_verdict: Omission would make later probabilistic execution appear licensed by feasible-set construction alone.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.swap_verdict: It follows incomplete databases because the unanswered question is now weighting rather than storage.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.entry_verdict: The inverse-problem framing gives reconstruction a precise connection to underidentification.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.exit_verdict: Pearl's intervention distinction prevents stress constraints from being presented as causal conditioning.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.promise_verdict: Stuart and partial-identification arguments retain their source and application limits.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.distinct_contribution_verdict: The section explains why a posterior is assumption-dependent even when observations are represented correctly.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.entry_belief: Alternative histories need explicit logical, economic and accounting meaning.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.open_question: What should a language contribute beyond a typed library and shared representation?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.parent_contribution: Rule and contract languages supply concrete alternatives and reusable semantic ideas.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.belief_update: Defaults, selected legal readings and contract state are distinct from uncertain history families and accounting treatment.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.exit_question: How much of the evidence entering these rules can document extraction supply?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.removal_verdict: Removal would leave the DSL proposal without a serious competitor or clear boundaries for imported semantics.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.swap_verdict: Language meaning sensibly precedes extraction because extracted content still needs an interpretation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.entry_verdict: The typed-library/shared-IR comparison keeps syntax preference from becoming a predetermined conclusion.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.exit_verdict: ACTUS and combinators distinguish contract meaning from valuation and recognition.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.promise_verdict: Catala and LegalMath are compared on their actual decision semantics, without a probability claim.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.distinct_contribution_verdict: Bounded generation is explicitly different from completeness over all economically possible histories.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.entry_belief: Rules and contracts require evidence whose financial context has survived extraction.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.open_question: Which extraction and reasoning results transfer to complete disclosure packages?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.parent_contribution: The section evaluates document tools against the representation's source and meaning requirements.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.belief_update: Table metrics and question-answering tasks measure scoped achievements, leaving company-history completeness unestablished.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.exit_question: Which solvers can execute the supported formal problems after interpretation?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.removal_verdict: Omitting this section would invite table-recognition performance to stand in for financial correctness.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.swap_verdict: It belongs after semantic alternatives so extraction is judged by the information those alternatives need.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.entry_verdict: The opening makes structure/content recognition distinct from accounting interpretation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.exit_verdict: Auditable RAG contributes persistent evidence and failure recovery without a local performance ranking.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.promise_verdict: TableFormer input text, predicted structure, correction operations and reported TEDS populations are kept separate.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:5.distinct_contribution_verdict: Docling version and licence distinctions address reuse; financial QA datasets address narrower retrieval/reasoning tasks.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.entry_belief: Extracted and interpreted disclosures can yield bounded logical and probabilistic models.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.open_question: What do available solvers establish about these models?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.parent_contribution: Solver scope and inference scope are related to the manuscript's exact accounting constraints.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.belief_update: Z3 supports the declared fragment; probabilistic execution separates the model from the algorithm used to explore it.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.exit_question: What integration problem remains after these component capabilities are acknowledged?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.removal_verdict: Removal would leave later solver choices vulnerable to a claim of arbitrary nonlinear tractability.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.swap_verdict: The section follows evidence interpretation because a solver cannot establish the meaning of its inputs.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.entry_verdict: The logical/linear restriction makes the relevant solver capability concrete.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.exit_verdict: Successful sampling still cannot establish exploration of every accounting interpretation.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.promise_verdict: Exact accounting constraints are not silently softened for library convenience.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:6.distinct_contribution_verdict: It distinguishes a valid encoded model, solver capability and adequate inference over that model.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.entry_belief: Several literatures support pieces of the design under different assumptions.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.open_question: What remains for AccDSL to establish as an integrated proposal?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.parent_contribution: The section joins disclosure, history, scenario, event, journal and statement responsibilities.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.belief_update: Integration must preserve the earlier distinctions and earn practical value through acceptance cases and comparison.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.exit_question: How does the proposed architecture allocate these responsibilities?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.removal_verdict: Removing the conclusion would leave a catalogue of sources without a consequence for the design.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.swap_verdict: Its integration claim needs the preceding component limits to avoid implying an established complete solution.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.entry_verdict: The remaining problem is framed as preservation of meaning across transitions.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.exit_verdict: The final comparative-evidence requirement makes the architecture chapter necessary without promising superiority.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.promise_verdict: The chapter closes its scoped-survey promise and leaves originality and empirical advantage unproved.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:7.distinct_contribution_verdict: This is the cross-literature synthesis, not a further component recommendation.

chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.entry_belief: Chapter 3 supplied concrete representation, correction and information-view requirements.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.open_question: Which researched methods support them, and which design responsibilities remain local?
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.parent_contribution: The survey connects accounting, databases, inference, languages, extraction and execution to the established needs.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.belief_update: Scoped component results can guide integration without proving whole-company coverage or practical advantage.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.exit_question: What architecture can preserve these boundaries from disclosure through future statements?
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.removal_verdict: Without the chapter, method selection and the DSL proposal would have no visible competing technical foundations.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.swap_verdict: The survey is intelligible after concrete cases and evidence requirements, before the proposed architecture.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.entry_verdict: The opening declares a design survey and its search-date boundary rather than an exhaustive result.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.exit_verdict: The concluding transition identifies integration as the unresolved engineering argument.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.promise_verdict: Adoption, adaptation and unsupported capabilities remain distinguishable throughout all six source families.
chapters/03-literature.tex:chapter:1.distinct_contribution_verdict: The chapter supplies reasons and limits for method choices; it does not substitute citation volume for validation.
